title: IllusionGameEEG_data
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography, physiological, and behavioral data collected from 103 healthy individuals (ages 21-45) during visual illusion perception tasks and resting-state recordings. Participants performed the Illusion Game task involving perceptual judgments on three classic visual illusions (Ebbinghaus, Müller-Lyer, and Vertical-Horizontal) with varying difficulty and illusion strength, followed by an 8-minute eyes-closed resting-state period. The dataset includes concurrent physiological monitoring (ECG, PPG, respiration) and behavioral responses, providing a comprehensive resource for investigating visual perception, illusion sensitivity, and associated neural and physiological correlates.
methods_description: EEG signals were recorded using a 64-channel EasyCap with BrainVision Recording system at 10,000 Hz sampling rate, with electrodes placed according to the 10-5 system and impedance maintained below 12 kOhm. Physiological signals (ECG, PPG, respiration) were acquired at 1,000 Hz using PLUX OpenSignals software and BITalino Toolkit. ECG was collected using modified Lead II configuration, respiration via abdominal belt, and PPG via finger clip on the non-dominant hand. The experimental protocol included 384 illusion trials (6 blocks of 64 trials each) and an 8-minute resting-state period with eyes closed.
